verdict: Moderna's revenue more than tripled to $389M on international vaccine deliveries, but a $0.9B litigation settlement charge drove a $1.3B net loss — without it, the loss would have been about $465M.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: vs -$2.52 a year ago; includes the $0.9B settlement charge

segments.name: Net product sales
segments.note: Vaccine sales — mainly COVID vaccines. Sales jumped on deliveries under long-term strategic partnerships with governments, including the first shipment under the U.K. partnership. Revenue was $78M in the U.S. and $311M international (including other revenue).

flow.costPlain: Making vaccines, excluding the litigation settlement shown separately below — including $38M of inventory write-downs and the cost of plant capacity kept ready for the fall season. As reported, total cost of sales was $955M.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: The labs: developing new vaccines and drugs. Down 24% — large Phase 3 respiratory programs and CMV studies wound down.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Sales teams, offices, admin. Down 18% on lower employee and marketing costs.

opex.name: Litigation settlement
opex.note: A one-time settlement charge Moderna booked inside cost of sales (in third-party royalties). Shown on its own line here so the vaccine business's own costs stay visible; the $950M cash payment followed in July 2026.

otherDetail: Interest income of $72M, less $18M of other expense — net $54M.
footerNote: As reported, cost of sales was $955M including the settlement.
follow100Note: For every $100 of revenue, the settlement charge alone consumed $226 — without it, Moderna's loss would have been about $119 per $100 of revenue, not $345. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: International partnerships delivered
takeaways.text: Revenue rose to $389M from $108M a year ago, with $311M earned internationally — COVID vaccine deliveries under long-term government partnerships, including the first U.K. shipment, did the work while the U.S. contributed $78M.

takeaways.title: The cost reset is real
takeaways.text: Excluding the settlement, costs fell across the board: R&D down 24% to $649M, SG&A down 18% to $173M, and underlying cost of sales down as unused-capacity costs and write-downs shrank. Moderna reiterated up to 10% revenue growth for 2026 with lower operating expenses.

takeaways.title: Two European approvals
takeaways.text: The EU approved mNEXSPIKE and mCOMBRIAX — the world's first flu-plus-COVID combination vaccine — and broadened mRESVIA's approval, while a Phase 3 trial of the intismeran cancer therapy in early-stage lung cancer began.

oneTimers: Cost of sales as reported was $955M, of which $878M was litigation settlement-related expense booked in third-party royalties (total royalties were $895M). The related $950M cash payment was made in July 2026, after this quarter ended.
Excluding the settlement charge, Moderna's net loss would have been about $465M instead of $1,343M.
